question: Which of the following is a straight-chain alkane containing 12 carbon atoms that are used as a major component in kerosene and some jet fuel research and also in the rubber and paper processing industry?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dodecane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dodecane (C₁₂H₂₆) is a straight-chain (n-alkane) hydrocarbon containing 12 carbon atoms, as indicated by the prefix "do-deca" (twelve). (डोडेकेन — 12 कार्बन परमाणु वाला ऐल्केन)

 

• It is a colourless liquid found as a component of kerosene and diesel fuel, and is studied as a component in jet fuel/alternative aviation fuel research.

 

• Dodecane and its derivatives (e.g., dodecanoic/lauric acid) are also used as raw materials in the rubber and paper processing industries, and in the manufacture of surfactants and plasticizers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alkane naming follows the number of carbon atoms: Undecane (11C), Dodecane (12C), Heptadecane (17C), Eicosane (20C) — all straight-chain (n-) alkanes belonging to the paraffin family.

 

NOTE

 

• Undecane (Option 1): An 11-carbon straight-chain alkane, not 12 carbons.

 

• Eicosane (Option 2): A 20-carbon straight-chain alkane (solid at room temperature), not 12 carbons.

 

• Heptadecane (Option 3): A 17-carbon straight-chain alkane, not 12 carbons.

question: Which of the following crops can be grown during the Kharif season in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cotton.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Cotton is a major Kharif crop in India, sown with the onset of the south-west monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn (September-October). (खरीफ फसल — कपास)

 

• Kharif crops require high temperature and abundant rainfall/moisture during their growing period; other examples include rice, maize, jowar, bajra, groundnut, soybean and sugarcane.

 

• Major cotton-growing states include Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rabi crops are sown in winter (October-December) and harvested in spring (March-April); they require cool climate and less water — examples include wheat, gram, mustard, barley and peas.

 

NOTE

 

• Gram (Option 1): A Rabi crop, sown in winter.

 

• Mustard (Option 2): A Rabi oilseed crop, sown in winter.

 

• Wheat (Option 3): India's principal Rabi cereal crop, sown in winter.

question: In which session of All India Congress Committee was the Quit India Resolution accepted?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Quit India Resolution was passed by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) at its session held in Bombay on 8 August 1942, at the Gowalia Tank Maidan (later renamed August Kranti Maidan). (भारत छोड़ो प्रस्ताव — बंबई अधिवेशन)

 

• Following the resolution, Mahatma Gandhi gave the call "Do or Die" and launched the Quit India Movement, demanding an immediate end to British rule in India.

 

• The entire top leadership of the Congress, including Gandhi and Nehru, was arrested by the British the very next morning (9 August 1942).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Quit India Movement is also known as the August Kranti (August Revolution).

 

NOTE

 

• Calcutta (Option 1): Site of earlier Congress sessions (e.g., the 1920 special session on Non-Cooperation), not the Quit India Resolution.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Not the venue of the Quit India Resolution.

 

• Madras (Option 3): Not the venue of the Quit India Resolution.

question: Jaimal and Patta were the warriors who were given charge of defending the fort of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chittor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jaimal Rathore and Patta (Fatta) Sisodia were Rajput warriors entrusted with the defence of the Chittorgarh Fort during its siege by Akbar in 1567-68. (जयमल और पत्ता — चित्तौड़गढ़ किले की रक्षा)

 

• Both warriors died fighting bravely; Akbar himself is said to have shot Jaimal with his matchlock Sangram during the siege.

 

• After the fort fell, Akbar had statues of Jaimal and Patta on elephants installed at the gates of the Agra Fort in honour of their valour.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The third Battle/Siege of Chittorgarh (1567-68) was Akbar's most famous campaign against the Sisodia rulers of Mewar; Rani Padmini's legendary Jauhar relates to an earlier siege by Alauddin Khilji (1303).

 

NOTE

 

• Raisen (Option 1): A separate fort in Madhya Pradesh, unrelated to Jaimal and Patta.

 

• Ajmer (Option 2): Not associated with Jaimal and Patta's defence.

 

• Udaipur (Option 3): Capital of Mewar founded later by Maharana Udai Singh II, not the fort defended by Jaimal and Patta.

question: What is the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)?
option_1: A region with a high annual rainfall
option_2: A low-pressure zone located at the equator
option_3: A zone where air tends to descend
option_4: A high-pressure zone located at the equator
solution_text:
The correct answer is A low-pressure zone located at the equator.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a belt of low pressure encircling the Earth near the equator, where the north-east and south-east trade winds converge. (अंतर-उष्णकटिबंधीय अभिसरण क्षेत्र — भूमध्य रेखा पर निम्न वायुदाब पेटी)

 

• It is also called the equatorial trough or the doldrums, characterised by intense heating, rising (ascending) air currents, and calm, light and variable winds.

 

• Because warm, moist air converges and rises here, the ITCZ is associated with heavy convectional rainfall, but the ITCZ itself is defined as the low-pressure convergence belt, not merely as "a region of high rainfall."

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ITCZ shifts seasonally — northward in the northern summer and southward in the northern winter — following the apparent movement of the sun, and this shift influences monsoon patterns including the Indian monsoon.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (high annual rainfall): A consequence/associated feature of the ITCZ, not its defining description.

 

• Option 3 (a zone where air tends to descend): Incorrect — air rises (ascends) in the ITCZ due to intense equatorial heating; descending air is characteristic of the subtropical high-pressure belts.

 

• Option 4 (a high-pressure zone at the equator): Incorrect — the ITCZ is a low-pressure, not high-pressure, zone.

question: Who among the following Indian grandmasters won the Bronze medal at FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Championship 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Savitha Shri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Savitha Shri B, an Indian Woman Grandmaster, won the Bronze medal in the Women's section at the FIDE World Rapid and Blitz Chess Championship 2022, held in Almaty, Kazakhstan. (सविता श्री — फिडे विश्व रैपिड और ब्लिट्ज़ शतरंज चैंपियनशिप 2022 कांस्य पदक)

 

• The championship is organised annually by the International Chess Federation (FIDE) and features separate Rapid and Blitz events for men and women.

 

• Savitha Shri B went on to become the 25th Woman Grandmaster of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indian chess players Koneru Humpy and Harika Dronavalli are established top Grandmasters who have won medals at various World Rapid/Blitz editions in other years.

 

NOTE

 

• Harika Dronavalli (Option 2): A leading Indian GM, but not the bronze medallist at the 2022 edition referred to here.

 

• Koneru Hampi (Option 3): [Koneru Humpy] A top Indian GM and former World Rapid Chess Champion, but not this event's bronze medallist.

 

• Tania Sachdev (Option 4): A well-known Indian Woman Grandmaster and commentator, not the bronze medallist at this event.

question: Who among the following is a famous music director?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khayyam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Khayyam (Mohammed Zahur Khayyam Hashmi) was a celebrated Indian music director/composer known for films like *Kabhi Kabhie*, *Umrao Jaan* and *Bazaar*. (ख़य्याम — प्रसिद्ध संगीत निर्देशक)

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (2011) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2010) for his contribution to Indian cinema.

 

• His compositions blended classical Indian music with Persian and folk influences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Khayyam's notable songs include those from *Umrao Jaan* (1981), for which he won the National Film Award for Best Music Direction.

 

NOTE

 

• Sameer (Option 2): A well-known Bollywood lyricist, not a music director.

 

• Anjaan (Option 3): A noted Bollywood lyricist, not a music director.

 

• Kaifi Azmi (Option 4): A renowned Urdu poet and lyricist, not a music director.

question: Mir Qasim name is associated with which of the following battles of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Battle of Buxar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Bengal, along with Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II, fought against the British East India Company in the Battle of Buxar (1764). (मीर कासिम — बक्सर का युद्ध)

 

• The British, led by Major Hector Munro, decisively defeated the combined forces, cementing British dominance over Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

• Mir Qasim had earlier been installed as Nawab of Bengal by the British (replacing Mir Jafar) but rebelled against their growing interference, leading to the conflict.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Treaty of Allahabad (1765), following the Battle of Buxar, granted the East India Company the Diwani rights (revenue collection) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.

 

NOTE

 

• Battle of Kirkee (Option 1): Fought in 1817 between the British and the Peshwa Baji Rao II during the Third Anglo-Maratha War, unrelated to Mir Qasim.

 

• Battle of Plassey (Option 3): Fought in 1757 between the British and Siraj-ud-Daulah (with Mir Jafar's betrayal), not Mir Qasim.

 

• Battle of Lahore (Option 4): Not associated with Mir Qasim.

question: What is the only sport specifically designed to be played by participants of both genders simultaneously?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Korfball.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Korfball is the only sport originally and specifically designed to be played by mixed-gender teams simultaneously — each team fields 4 men and 4 women on court at the same time. (कोर्फबॉल — दोनों लिंगों द्वारा एक साथ खेला जाने वाला एकमात्र खेल)

 

• It was invented in 1902 by Nico Broekhuysen, a Dutch schoolteacher, and is popular in the Netherlands, Belgium and Taiwan.

 

• It resembles a mix of basketball and netball, played with a ball and korf (basket) mounted on a pole, without a backboard.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Korfball is governed internationally by the International Korfball Federation (IKF).

 

NOTE

 

• Netball (Option 1): Traditionally played predominantly by women; not designed for simultaneous mixed-gender play.

 

• Quidditch (Option 2): A fictional sport from the Harry Potter series; its real-world adaptation (now called quadball) does have mixed-gender rules but is not the sport specifically referenced as "the only" one originally designed for this purpose.

 

• Basketball (Option 4): Played separately by men's and women's teams, not designed for simultaneous mixed play.

question: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation), formed in 1985, has eight member states: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan (joined 2007). (सार्क — दक्षिण एशियाई क्षेत्रीय सहयोग संगठन)

 

• Myanmar is NOT a member of SAARC; instead, it is a member of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) and ASEAN.

 

• SAARC's headquarters (Secretariat) is located in Kathmandu, Nepal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• China, USA, Japan, and the EU hold Observer status in SAARC.

 

NOTE

 

• Pakistan (Option 1): A founding member of SAARC.

 

• Afghanistan (Option 3): Joined SAARC as its eighth member in 2007.

 

• Bhutan (Option 4): A founding member of SAARC.

question: With a stretch of about 724 km, which river is one of the most important rivers of peninsular India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tapi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tapi (Tapti) River is about 724 km long and is one of the major west-flowing rivers of peninsular India, along with the Narmada. (तापी नदी — प्रायद्वीपीय भारत की प्रमुख नदी)

 

• It originates in the Satpura Range in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, and flows westward through Maharashtra and Gujarat before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

 

• Along with the Narmada, it flows through a rift valley between the Satpura and Vindhya/Satmala ranges, unlike most peninsular rivers which flow eastward into the Bay of Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major dams on the Tapi include the Ukai Dam in Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Beas (Option 2): A Himalayan (north Indian) river, a tributary of the Sutlej, not a peninsular river.

 

• Palar (Option 3): A much shorter south Indian river (about 348 km) flowing through Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

 

• Bhavani (Option 4): A tributary of the Kaveri in Tamil Nadu, much shorter than 724 km.

question: The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill 2022 proposed to convert __________ as Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya.
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Rail and Transportation Institute.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Universities (Amendment) Bill, 2022 proposed converting the National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI), Vadodara, into a Central University named "Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya (GSV)". (गति शक्ति विश्वविद्यालय — नेशनल रेल एंड ट्रांसपोर्टेशन इंस्टीट्यूट)

 

• The move aligns with the government's PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, aimed at creating a skilled workforce for the transport and logistics sector.

 

• NRTI was originally established in 2018 as a specialised institute for railway and transportation-related education and research.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya is envisioned as a multidisciplinary university covering railways, roads, ports, aviation, and other transport and logistics domains.

 

NOTE

 

• National Infrastructure and Industrial Institute (Option 1): Not the institute referenced in the Bill.

 

• National Energy and Environment Institute (Option 2): Not the institute referenced in the Bill.

 

• National Transport and Infrastructure Institute (Option 4): A distractor with a similar-sounding but incorrect name; the actual institute is the National Rail and Transportation Institute.

question: What is the change in fiscal deficit if both the primary deficit and interest payments are doubled?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increase by 100%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fiscal Deficit = Primary Deficit + Interest Payments. (राजकोषीय घाटा = प्राथमिक घाटा + ब्याज भुगतान)

 

• If both the primary deficit (PD) and interest payments (IP) are doubled, the new fiscal deficit becomes 2×PD + 2×IP = 2×(PD + IP) = 2 × (original fiscal deficit).

 

• Doubling a quantity means it becomes 200% of the original, i.e., it increases by 100% over the original value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest payments; it indicates the borrowing requirement excluding interest obligations on past debt.

 

NOTE

 

• Increase by 200% (Option 2): Incorrect — this would imply the deficit becomes triple (300% of) the original, not double.

 

• Decrease by 50% (Option 3): Incorrect — doubling both components increases, not decreases, the fiscal deficit.

 

• Decrease by 100% (Option 4): Incorrect — this would imply the deficit becomes zero, which is not the case.

question: In any economy, the income velocity of the hoarded money (idle) by the public is equal to______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is zero.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Velocity of money measures the rate at which money changes hands (circulates) in the economy through transactions. (मुद्रा का वेग — जमाखोरी की गई राशि के लिए शून्य)

 

• Hoarded (idle) money is money that the public holds but does not spend or circulate — it sits idle rather than being used for transactions.

 

• Since hoarded money does not change hands at all, its income velocity of circulation is zero.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Fisher's Equation of Exchange (MV = PT) relates money supply (M), velocity (V), price level (P) and transactions (T); a fall in velocity due to hoarding can dampen aggregate demand even if money supply is constant.

 

NOTE

 

• One (Option 1): Would imply the money is used exactly once in the period, which does not describe idle/hoarded money.

 

• Greater than one (Option 2): Describes actively circulating money used in multiple transactions, the opposite of hoarded money.

 

• Greater than zero (Option 4): Incorrect — hoarded money, by definition, does not circulate at all, so its velocity is exactly zero, not merely "greater than zero."

question: Who, in the 1860s, undertook a thorough investigation of the gas laws expressing the relationships of pressure, temperature and volume in carbon dioxide?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thomas Andrews.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thomas Andrews, an Irish chemist and physicist, conducted detailed experiments in the 1860s on the relationship between pressure, temperature and volume of carbon dioxide (CO₂). (थॉमस एंड्रयूज — कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड की क्रांतिक अवस्था)

 

• His work led to the discovery of the critical point/critical temperature of a gas — the temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied by pressure alone, regardless of how much pressure is applied.

 

• Andrews's 1869 paper "On the Continuity of the Gaseous and Liquid States of Matter" is considered a landmark in the study of the liquefaction of gases.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The critical temperature of CO₂ is about 31.1°C, above which it exists only as a gas irrespective of pressure.

 

NOTE

 

• Giulio Natta (Option 2): An Italian chemist known for work on polymers (Nobel Prize 1963), unrelated to CO₂ gas laws.

 

• John Dalton (Option 3): Known for Atomic Theory and Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures (early 1800s), not this 1860s CO₂ investigation.

 

• Marguerite Perey (Option 4): A French physicist who discovered the element francium (1939), unrelated to this work.

question: Which cell analysis technique is used to rapidly analyse single cells or particles as they flow through single or multiple lasers while suspended in a buffered salt-based solution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flow cytometry.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Flow cytometry is a laboratory technique that rapidly analyses the physical and chemical characteristics of single cells or particles as they flow, one at a time, through one or more laser beams, while suspended in a buffered salt-based (saline) solution. (फ्लो साइटोमेट्री — एकल कोशिका विश्लेषण तकनीक)

 

• Light scattered and fluorescence emitted by each cell as it passes the laser is detected to determine properties such as cell size, granularity, and specific molecular markers (e.g., surface proteins tagged with fluorescent antibodies).

 

• It is widely used in immunology, haematology and cancer diagnostics (e.g., for CD4 cell counts in HIV monitoring).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• A related instrument, the fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS), extends flow cytometry by physically sorting cells based on their measured characteristics.

 

NOTE

 

• Mass spectroscopy (Option 1): Identifies substances based on the mass-to-charge ratio of ions, not single-cell laser-based flow analysis.

 

• Electrochemical analysis (Option 3): Measures electrical properties (current, potential) of chemical reactions, unrelated to laser-based single-cell analysis.

 

• Multiple displacement amplification (Option 4): A DNA amplification technique used to amplify small amounts of genomic DNA, not a cell-flow analysis technique.

question: ________ won the bronze medal in the women's 10 m air rifle event at the ISSF World Cup 2023 in Cairo, Egypt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tilottama Sen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tilottama Sen, a young Indian shooter, won the bronze medal in the women's 10 m air rifle event at the ISSF World Cup 2023 held in Cairo, Egypt. (तिलोत्तमा सेन — आईएसएसएफ विश्व कप 2023 काहिरा कांस्य पदक)

 

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) World Cup is a premier international shooting circuit that also serves as a qualification pathway for events like the Olympic Games.

 

• India had a strong showing at the Cairo 2023 World Cup, with medals across rifle, pistol and shotgun events, including a gold in men's 10 m air rifle by Rudrankksh Patil.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 10 m air rifle event is shot at a target 10 metres away using a compressed-air/CO₂-powered rifle.

 

NOTE

 

• Sift Kaur Samra (Option 1): An accomplished Indian rifle shooter, but not the bronze medallist in this specific event at Cairo 2023.

 

• Shreyasi Singh (Option 3): An Indian shotgun (double trap) shooter, unrelated to the 10 m air rifle event.

 

• Nivetha Paramanantham (Option 4): An Indian shooter, but not the bronze medallist in this specific event at Cairo 2023.

question: Lui Ngai Ni is a festival that is associated with which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lui-Ngai-Ni is a traditional seed-sowing festival celebrated by the Naga tribes of Manipur, typically held around 15 February every year. (लुई-नगाई-नी — मणिपुर का बीज बुवाई उत्सव)

 

• It marks the beginning of the agricultural season and is celebrated with traditional dances, songs, and rituals by various Naga tribes across Manipur.

 

• The festival is also observed as a symbol of unity among the Naga community and is a recognised state festival of Manipur.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important festivals of Manipur include Yaoshang (a Holi-related festival) and Sangai Festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Not associated with Lui-Ngai-Ni.

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Not associated with Lui-Ngai-Ni.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Not associated with Lui-Ngai-Ni.

question: Gulabo Sapera is associated to which of the following dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gulabo Sapera is a renowned Indian folk dancer credited with popularising the Kalbelia dance of Rajasthan on national and international stages. (गुलाबो सपेरा — कालबेलिया नृत्य)

 

• Kalbelia is a folk dance performed by the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community of Rajasthan, characterised by swirling black skirts and snake-like movements of the dancers.

 

• Kalbelia dance and songs of Rajasthan were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gulabo Sapera was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2016 for her contribution to Kalbelia dance.

 

NOTE

 

• Sattriya (Option 1): A classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras).

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 2): A classical dance form of Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Pandavani (Option 4): A folk narrative singing style of Chhattisgarh, based on the Mahabharata, not Gulabo Sapera's dance form.

question: The measures of money supply, namely, M1, M2, M3 and M4, in this order, indicate:
option_4: decreasing order of store of value
solution_text:
The correct answer is decreasing order of liquidity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) classifies money supply into four measures — M1, M2, M3 and M4 — arranged in decreasing order of liquidity. (मुद्रा आपूर्ति के माप — तरलता के घटते क्रम में)

 

• M1 (currency with public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI) is the most liquid; M4 (M3 + total post office deposits) is the least liquid.

 

• As we move from M1 to M4, progressively less liquid assets (like time deposits and post office savings) are added, so liquidity decreases while the components become better stores of value over longer terms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• M3 (Broad Money) = M1 + time deposits with banks, is the most commonly used measure of money supply for monetary policy purposes in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Decreasing order of earning capacity (Option 1): Incorrect — the sequence reflects liquidity, not earning/interest capacity (in fact, less liquid components like time deposits typically earn more interest).

 

• Increasing order of liquidity (Option 2): Incorrect — it is the reverse; liquidity decreases, not increases, from M1 to M4.

 

• Decreasing order of store of value (Option 4): Incorrect — in fact, store-of-value capacity tends to increase from M1 to M4, opposite of what is stated.

question: Which of the following is a feature of the Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Are non-justiciable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), given in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Indian Constitution, are non-justiciable — they are not enforceable by any court of law. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — गैर-न्यायोचित)

 

• Despite being non-justiciable, DPSPs are declared "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37), and it is the duty of the State to apply them while making laws.

 

• They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution and aim to establish a welfare state by promoting social and economic democracy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Unlike DPSPs, Fundamental Rights (Part III) are justiciable — a citizen can move the courts (including directly the Supreme Court under Article 32) for their enforcement.

 

NOTE

 

• Are available against state (Option 2): This describes Fundamental Rights, not DPSPs, which are directives/guidelines to the state rather than rights enforceable against it.

 

• Can be suspended during emergency (Option 3): It is certain Fundamental Rights (e.g., under Article 19) that can be suspended during a National Emergency, not the DPSPs.

 

• Are negative in nature (Option 4): Fundamental Rights are often described as largely negative (restraining the state); DPSPs are positive in nature, directing the state to take affirmative action.

question: From which five-year plan onwards in India, were fiscal and economic reforms including liberalization adopted?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighth Five Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's major economic reforms — Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization (LPG) — were launched in 1991 under the government of P.V. Narasimha Rao with Dr. Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister. (आठवीं पंचवर्षीय योजना — उदारीकरण)

 

• These reforms coincided with, and were institutionalised through, the Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-1997), which focused on human resource development, controlling population growth, and market-oriented reforms.

 

• The Eighth Plan is regarded as the plan that formally embraced structural adjustment, fiscal correction, and opening up of the Indian economy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Eighth Plan could not start on time in 1990 due to political instability, so it was delayed and finally launched in 1992; the years 1990-92 are known as the Plan Holiday period.

 

NOTE

 

• Seventh Five Year Plan (Option 2): 1985-1990, predates the 1991 reforms.

 

• Sixth Five Year Plan (Option 3): 1980-1985, predates the 1991 reforms.

 

• Ninth Five Year Plan (Option 4): 1997-2002, came after reforms were already adopted in the Eighth Plan.

question: Usually, the reduction in the taxes will have ________ multiplier effect compared to an increase in government spending on aggregate demand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is smaller.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The tax multiplier is generally smaller in magnitude than the government spending multiplier. (कर गुणक — सरकारी व्यय गुणक से छोटा)

 

• When government spending increases, the entire amount enters the economy directly as demand; but when taxes are cut, households save a portion of the extra disposable income (based on the Marginal Propensity to Consume), so less of the tax cut actually translates into new spending.

 

• As a result, an equivalent-sized tax cut has a smaller effect on aggregate demand than an equivalent increase in government spending.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Government spending multiplier = 1/(1-MPC), while the Tax multiplier = -MPC/(1-MPC), which is smaller in absolute value for the same MPC.

 

NOTE

 

• No multiplier effect (Option 1): Incorrect — a tax cut does have some multiplier effect, just a smaller one.

 

• Higher multiplier effect (Option 3): Incorrect — this reverses the actual relationship; the tax multiplier is smaller, not higher.

 

• Equivalent multiplier effect (Option 4): Incorrect — the two multipliers are not equal because a spending increase directly injects the full amount, unlike a tax cut.

question: Which of the following statements about fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution is FALSE?
option_1: They provide necessary conditions for moral protection.
option_2: The lay down the foundation for social justice.
option_3: They provide necessary conditions for material protection.
option_4: They provide necessary conditions for practicing untouchability.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They provide necessary conditions for practicing untouchability.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Rights (Part III of the Constitution) protect citizens from various social evils rather than enabling them. (मौलिक अधिकार — अस्पृश्यता का उन्मूलन)

 

• Article 17 of the Indian Constitution specifically abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form, making it a punishable offence.

 

• Therefore, the statement that Fundamental Rights "provide necessary conditions for practicing untouchability" is factually FALSE — they do the exact opposite, i.e., they prohibit it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights genuinely do provide the necessary conditions for material and moral development of individuals and lay the foundation for social justice, consistent with the other three statements being true.

 

NOTE

 

• They provide necessary conditions for moral protection (Option 1): A true statement — Fundamental Rights (e.g., Right to Freedom of Religion, Right to Life with dignity) support moral development, so it is not the false statement.

 

• They lay down the foundation for social justice (Option 2): A true statement — rights like equality (Articles 14-18) aim at social justice, so it is not the false statement.

 

• They provide necessary conditions for material protection (Option 3): A true statement — rights protect citizens' material/economic interests (e.g., against exploitation under Articles 23-24), so it is not the false statement.

question: Indian Classical dancer Kumkum Dhar was awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2020 for her contribution to _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kumkum Dhar is an eminent Indian classical dancer honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for the year 2020 for her contribution to Kathak. (कुमकुम धर — कथक नृत्य)

 

• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, characterised by intricate footwork, spins (chakkars) and storytelling (through mime and expression), with roots in the temples and courts of North India.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, confers its annual Akademi Puraskar to recognise outstanding contributions to the performing arts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards for 2019, 2020 and 2021 were announced together in a later ceremony.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 1): A classical dance form of Odisha, not Kumkum Dhar's field.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 2): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, not Kumkum Dhar's field.

 

• Manipuri (Option 4): A classical dance form of Manipur, not Kumkum Dhar's field.
